reviews.review: Amazing gunplay, good visuals, great community (yes even the toxic ones, they're necessary) and stunning audio design. ARC Raiders is peak.

Unless they implement a PvP consent system (I'd really like one similar to Fallout 76), I just can't justify spending time playing. I'd even take a PvE only queue.

Before I quit, most of the games I was getting were shoot-on-sight within a minute of spawning, and multiple teams converging in one spot right away, so no one has any loot, and it's a complete waste of time and ammo - very sad to see.

I really enjoyed the first week of the game's release with a lot of friendly / interesting people in comms. IMO, you need casual / friendly players who won't immediately shoot on site for it to actually remain a healthy PvPvE, and to get the most entertaining interactions. 

Otherwise, the game is visually stunning, has awesome enemies, and feels fantastic to play. I just wish people weren't speedrunning it, considering not everyone is going to be on the same skill level (I suck).

I never thought I would like an extraction shooter, but [b]damn[/b], Arc Raiders is good. 

If you feel like you wouldn't like extraction shooters, then I would absolutely give Arc Raiders a try.

I'VE FIGURED IT OUT

This is a gambling game disguised as a looter shooter.

Select no loadout no weapons or items, the game spawns you in the middle of nowhere, takes a while and eventually you will find very basic items.

Go in with a risky load out- better loot
More risk = more reward.

So what's the catch?
When you eventually run out of your good loot (you will as enemies are OP and it takes days to reload) you can go to the store and buy the in game currency.

Oh you can grind but the aim of the game is to spend spend spend, do you value your time? well just spend some cash. Don't value your time? spend hours grinding.

But out of all of this, you claw and grasp for some fun, there's VERY little of it. I went in to give it a fair chance but after testing my theory it's sad, it's a free to play game with a £30 starting fee, very sad.

Leaving my original review at the bottom, this game is definitely a thumbs up, for $40 now that they have addressed things like matchmaking and cheating better the game is a %100 worthwhile purchase.
Cheaters and matchmaking go hand in hand for why I think this game is good in spite of streamer opinions and my own previous opinion, the matchmaking both allows you to play this game as a PvE game with a bit of extra tension, but it also allows the cheaters to be fed in to the top skill pvp lobbies, meaning %99 of the non streamer playerbase will never see them.
If you are a shooter pro and have perfect game sense and reflexes, the game may not be for you, if you are someone with a life who wants a fun game they can jump indo and out of for an hour session after work, this is your game.

I've been loosely following this game since it was announced years ago. Even though it became a PvP game at some point during development, I thought I'd give it a try when I heard most of the community around the game was quite friendly. 

I don't usually go for PvP games but I had hope that it would be a fun time, at least for the first few months after release. I was mostly right. I've had plenty of great interactions with random people. But the game has devolved into a free-for-all, especially since the first new map released, and the friendly interactions almost completely stopped months earlier than I thought they would. 

The game itself is really fun. The enemies are all interesting and have different weaknesses and strengths to them which makes each encounter a tactical challenge. The loot is very rewarding, with many unique weapons and gadgets for countering the different ARCs and other players. The different map modifiers can completely change the map they're affecting and how you would go about a normal run, making them some of the most rewarding and entertaining matches. I love the gameplay loop of scavenging different locations, fighting though the patrolling ARCs to the extraction points and getting out before you get beat.

I honestly think the weakest point of the game is the other players in the matches. There's no worse feeling in this game than gearing up to fight a tough enemy or boss, only to get shot 3 seconds after you spawn and lose everything you'd gathered over the previous hours. 

I understand that that's part of the appeal of "Extraction shooters", but I just feel like ARC Raiders would massively benefit from heavily dissuading, but not disabling, PvP outside of certain maps or modifiers.

Also the AI generated voice "performances" completely annihilate any investment or interest you could have in the characters/vendors. There was no reason to not record voice actors for the actual characters at the very least.

I genuinely love ARC Raiders. The core game loop is incredibly addictive, honestly, even satisfying. There’s something special about the rhythm the game creates, and for a long time it kept me completely hooked.

But as time goes on, it’s becoming more and more noticeable that the player base is shifting toward toxic, hyper-competitive gameplay. Since PvP is basically the main form of player interaction, the game ends up feeling like a constant ambush simulator. For some people, that’s fantastic. But for me, the most memorable moments in ARC Raiders were the ones where I teamed up with total strangers to take down massive, terrifying robotic forces, moments where everyone worked together toward a shared goal: survive.

There’s nothing like the feeling of saving a random player from a lethal encounter… or being saved yourself at the last second. That sense of spontaneous cooperation is what made the game feel alive.

Unfortunately, the recent matches just don’t feel rewarding anymore. You load into a map and everyone’s hiding in corners like rats, waiting to shoot you in the back and loot your gear. The snowball effect is brutal, you end up feeling forced to play the same way just to maintain a viable economy. Emotionally, it gets draining: you shoot players who never even saw you, or someone you never saw wipes you out instantly and you lose everything.

This loop becomes genuinely frustrating, and you can see other players mentioning it in their comments too. The game itself isn’t bad, far from it, but it feels like if you don’t join the culture of camping and preying on other players, you’re always at a disadvantage. If you want to be a peaceful or cooperative player, there’s less and less room for that, and hostile players face almost no consequences.

ARC Raiders is still a good game with a lot of potential, but looking at the bigger picture, there are many other games that offer a less frustrating experience, ones that feel more worth investing your time and money into.

I love looter shooters. I love PVP. I love that the AI enemy is a good level of difficult. And I really enjoyed this game for the first few weeks.

However, some penalty needs to be had in PVP during big bot maps. Queen and Matriarch (for now.) The secret sauce for Extraction Shooters is a good balance between risk and reward. Right now, there is an imbalance against the big bots. If I go in with guns to do damage against big bots, I am automatically more likely to die if a player decides to shoot me. From this, the risk is higher than the reward of a couple matriarch/queen cores.

I am not saying PVP should be removed from those events, but a penalty or a risk against them needs to be added in. Right now they have all the advantage and very little risk to go around killing players with Jupiters/Hull Crackers, Etc.

This game has the potential to be one of the best extractions shooters that could do something that I had never experienced before. The PVE Gameplay is exquisite. The ARC/AI enemies in the game require skill and nuance to fight.

PVP is not fun. Gunplay VS another person is a game of who is best geared and shot first. Due to PVP existing, enemy players will camp extractions, and pretend to not be aggressive in order to shoot you in the back whenever possible. The reward for this is minimal, as the player who won the gunfight already has better equipment than you, and likely can use none of the items you have scavenged during the game.

Escape From Tarkov offers a more realistic and hardcore experience. Hunt Showdown offers a much better PVP gun fight experience. Arc Raiders could be an unmatched PVE Extraction experience.

EDIT: Jan 28th, 2026

My review has been updated to be recommended, as aggression based matchmaking does help to offer a more catered experience for players who do prefer a more PVP-based game, or a more PVE-focused experience. While opting completely out of PVP is still not possible, and the weekends tend to be a more aggressive experience, Arc Raiders feels like a better experience for a PVE focused player, specifically when disabling Cross-Play.

Worth it to pick up this one though.

This game is excellent for what it is shown as, an atmospheric Sci-Fi extraction shooter where humans face extinction by robot invaders in a post-civilization world. I have sunk many hours into both solo and team play, and at it's core, the game is an incredible PvPvE experience. 

However, there is one big tumor that will eventually kill the game's (lore accurate) culture if left unchecked. 
PvP players will eventually kill off the stranger goodwill that the game launched with.
 
Solo play within the first few weeks of launch was incredible, 9 out of 10 raids I was never attacked by other players and we all understood ARC as the real threat. 
Now, it's too easy to just shoot another solo in the back for some easy loot, and this is happening much more often than before. 
(Team play is usually kill-on-sight; this is much more expected and not a major issue.)

The fix for this is to implement a complex matchmaking system of sorts; not by gear or player level, but by things such a player's ratio of shooting another first, or a player's average choice to seek out fights over things like quests or loot. 
This will allow aggressive players to play with other aggressive players, rats to play with other rats, and peaceful players with other peaceful players.

Otherwise, aggressive players and rats will drive the peaceful community away and and ARC raiders will suffer the same problem that every other extraction shooter suffers from, and the player base will eventually stagnate.
It isn't an easy thing to create such a system, but the tools are there, and the devs have both the player data and technical ability to do so.
This would likely lead to longer queue times and emptier lobbies in the short term, but the alternative will drain the playerbase of casual and friendly players anyways, and leave only a punishing experience for anybody new or returning.

TLDR; Awesome game at the core, but intricate matchmaking must be introduced, otherwise the game will stagnate at the hands of PVP tryhards.
